questions.answer: Easy. The host university kept me updated with arrival information during the weeks leading up my arrival.

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. I recieved an email presenting two housing options and how/when to apply.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In my experience, it was nice living off campus and closer to the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing is very expensive compared to the quality. If I'd known this beforehand, I would have considered finding a shared appartment in the city, as you can get it cheaper or at the same price. Student housing in the UK is very low quality compared to Denmark. There are no proper areas for social gatherings, and the buildings are old and in a poor state. Eg. the windows in the kitchen couldn't be opened fully, only ajar, and the ventilation didn't work. Due to this, the kithcen would be very hot and stinky very quickly. Also, my room was 5 meters from the railway, so I had a hard time studying in my room during the day due to trains coming by my window every 5min. I was also woken up every night by the noisy freight trains, and therefore hand a poor quality of sleep during my stay. On a positive note, there wes a cleaning staff cleaning the kitchen every two weeks (though they sometimes forgot), and there was a team of guards checking on us daily. Also, it was easy to get in contact with the staff if we had any problems regarding the housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was difficult finding information such as courses and projects on the uni website, and we had to contact the uni and make them create a special project unit for us exchange students, as the ones they offered didn't fit UCPH's expectations. Also, there was a lot of miscommunitation between UCPH and my host institution, which was very difficult to navigate in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
I had a contact person in the UK helping with any information I was missing. This was nice as some of the information from the application guidance on
ku.net
was scattered on the website and hard to find.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Completely successful. It was a bit hard to navigate in at first, but I had some help from my UK contact person and a danish post-exhange student. I also had the opportunity to reregister for other courses opun arrivival if I had changed my mind.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress. It might be difficult to navigate in all the information given, but it is in the host institutions interest that you arrive, and they will do everything in their power to help you through the application process if only you answer their mails and follow their advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wrote my bachelor thesis during my stay, and I was very satisfied with the project and the guidance I got from my supervisor.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Besides my bachelor thesis, I took two courses. One BA course with an oral presentation as the exam, and one MA course with a written exam. The BA course was easy, with no high expectations for the final product. The MA course was difficult, but with a level similar to UCPH courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching was very similar, though they used scientific articles as background littereature instead of books. The lectures were recorded which was nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Bachelor thesis (18ECTS)
Global Health and Management, BA (6ECTS)
The Molecular Biology and Treatment of Cancer, MA (6ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Global health course is a good choice for exchange students as it is almost impossible to fail. The cancer course was super interesting but also difficult, so I would maybe recommend taking another, easier course (eg. a course you have already taken in UCPH) so you have more time to enjoy your stay.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were many clubs, sports and other social activities to join.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you can imagine. They had it all.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a sport or any other of you hobbies. It is a great way of getting in touch with people from your host country.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city of Bath. It has a lot of cute streets, areas and nice cafés. There are a lot of great hiking areas in southern England. I went to down to the coast (durdle door), the city cheddar at it's caves as well as a few trips to Wales were there are great hiking trails as well. As for cities, there are a lot of small very cute picturesque cities around Bath like Castle Combe or Lacock. Finally, Bath is only a few hours away from London and Oxford.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: They are very open, helpful and not that different from Danes. You won't have a problem adjusting to the culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join a society.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are always super helpful and polite.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware that most of the international students are around 20 years old and not always very mature. If you wish to avoid this, consider finding a shared apartment in the city, eg. though Facebook pages.
Find out if you are doing the exchange for social or academic purposes. If social, consider taking easier courses as it will give you more time away from you studies.
Enjoy it while it lasts, it will go by fast :)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My bachelor thesis and the collaboration I had with my supervisor.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The poor housing and young international students who weren't super mature.
